text: Trump campaign star Conway named as his presidential counselor. WASHINGTON (Reuters) - In a stunning turn of events, Kellyanne Conway, the Republican pollster who played a pivotal role in transforming Donald Trump’s chaotic campaign into a disciplined powerhouse, is set to become White House counselor when he assumes office next month. In this crucial new role, Conway will be at the epicenter of Trump’s administration, wielding significant influence over messaging and legislative priorities, as confirmed by the transition team in a dramatic statement on Thursday. They hailed Conway, 49, as the groundbreaking first woman campaign manager to steer a victorious U.S. presidential campaign. In a bold move, Trump has also appointed three die-hard loyalists to take the reins of his communications team. The Republican National Committee’s Sean Spicer is stepping in as press secretary, while Hope Hicks, Jason Miller, and Dan Scavino join the ranks of this high-stakes communications team. Throughout the tumultuous lead-up to the Nov. 8 election and beyond, Conway has been a ubiquitous figure on U.S. television news, often thrust into the spotlight to defend or elucidate Trump’s controversial decisions. Trump himself declared, “Conway played a crucial role in my victory,” in the transition team’s statement, describing her as a relentless and formidable advocate for his agenda, with unparalleled insights into effectively communicating their message. Trump, the business mogul from New York, is set to take the reins on Jan. 20. In a captivating interview with ABC’s “Good Morning America” shortly after the bombshell announcement, Conway was grilled about when Trump would hold his first news conference. She skillfully dodged the question, leaving viewers on the edge of their seats. Despite holding several rallies since his election triumph, Trump has yet to face formal questions from the press, raising eyebrows across the nation. He shockingly canceled a Dec. 15 news conference that was supposed to unveil his plans for managing his extensive business empire while in the White House, promising to reschedule for January. Conway revealed to ABC that Trump is laser-focused on assembling his Cabinet. “He’s been very busy doing that,” she said, hinting at the whirlwind of activity behind the scenes. Given her prominent position in the campaign and transition team, speculation has run rampant regarding what position Conway, a seasoned political strategist, would occupy in Trump’s administration. In a revealing moment, Conway, a devoted mother of four, admitted that she didn’t immediately accept an early offer during the transition because she had to carefully consider her family responsibilities. “I would say that I don’t play golf and I don’t have a mistress so, I have a lot of time that a lot of these other men don’t,” Conway candidly told Fox Business Network. “I see people on the weekend spending an awful lot of time on their golf games and that’s their right, but the kids will be with me, we live in the same house, and they come first.”

text: Italy's center-right in search of a leader as election nears. ROME (Reuters) - In a shocking turn of events, former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi has stormed back into the chaotic arena of Italian politics, boldly declaring his intention to lead a revitalized center-right into the high-stakes national elections looming early next year. At precisely the same moment, Berlusconi's fiery ally, Matteo Salvini, was passionately rallying his Northern League party and making an audacious bid to claim the prime ministership for himself. Salvini Premier read a sign stuck to the lectern. However, in a twist that could unsettle the entire political landscape, neither leader appears likely to ascend to the government’s highest office even if they manage to clinch an election victory, with alternative candidates already starting to bubble up to the surface. An apparent power struggle is brewing between Berlusconi and Salvini, but fear not, political experts say—this clash won’t spiral out of control. They recognize that a brutal showdown would spell disaster with voters, warned Piero Ignazi, a politics professor at Bologna University. The stark reality is that both men are set to remain at the helm of their respective parties, but neither is on track to become the next prime minister, he stated ominously. This scenario paves the way for a consensus candidate who must navigate the enormous rifts between the three dominant rightist factions—from the fiercely anti-EU stance of both the Northern League and Brothers of Italy to Berlusconi's surprisingly pro-European rhetoric expressed just days ago. Latest opinion polls reveal that this trio of long-time allies is surging ahead, projected to secure a formidable 35 percent of the vote, with the anti-migrant Northern League slightly leading Berlusconi’s Forza Italia at around 15 percent. In stark contrast, the anti-establishment 5-Star Movement and the beleaguered ruling center-left Democratic Party (PD) are floundering at roughly 28 percent each. The 5-Star has firmly dismissed any possibility of coalition alliances, while the center-left's voting pool continues to dwindle, plagued by vicious infighting among various leftist factions. Under the current electoral system, no party or coalition appears poised to claim enough seats to govern independently. However, political analysts are buzzing with excitement, claiming that the winds are finally filling the sails of the center-right after years of stagnation, creating a pre-election tidal wave of momentum. Berlusconi, who infamously resigned in disgrace during the 2011 sovereign debt crisis, has been marred by scandals and legal troubles ever since, culminating in his expulsion from the Senate and a ban from running for office due to a 2013 tax fraud conviction. Following life-threatening open heart surgery last year, many analysts had penned his political obituary. Yet, in a stunning comeback that defies expectations, the media tycoon, now 81, is once again making waves and has launched an appeal to the European Court of Human Rights to overturn his election ban. A hearing is set for November, but a verdict could be months away, leaving him almost certainly unable to participate in the next national vote, which is due by May 2018 and anticipated to take place in March. Despite his advanced age, Berlusconi is itching to reclaim the prime ministership. This may be his final chance at glory. But realistically speaking, it’s not looking promising, admitted a Forza Italia official, who preferred to remain anonymous due to the explosive nature of the topic. Notably, Berlusconi delivered his electrifying political comeback speech at an event hosted by Forza Italia stalwart Antonio Tajani, the president of the European Parliament. Sources within the party suggest Tajani is the frontrunner to step into the role of Berlusconi’s surrogate. While Berlusconi’s name abroad conjures up scandalous memories of infamous 'bunga bunga' parties and cheeky remarks, Tajani presents as a far more subdued figure, whose pro-European leanings would likely reassure international markets. Yet, these very inclinations could spell trouble for Berlusconi’s hardline allies, who have consistently railed against the European Union and fervently called for Italy to abandon the euro. "The leader of the center-right needs to be chosen through a clear process, perhaps a primary," declared Giorgia Meloni, head of Brothers of Italy, during an explosive interview with Sky Italia television on Sunday. "I imagine that whatever grassroots method you decide, Tajani will not win out," she warned.

'We have more than enough to worry about in our daily lives. Personally, I’m more anxious about how much it’s going to cost me to put food on the table (than North Korea),' exclaimed You, from Sejong city in central South Korea. 'Talk of North Korea honestly feels distant to me!'      For most ordinary South Koreans, who have lived under the shadow of war with their hostile, now nuclear-armed neighbor for decades, it is the more mundane concerns that keep them awake at night - jobs, the economy, and the intense pressures that have surged alongside South Korea’s rapid development since the end of fighting with the North in 1953. It’s shocking to note that evidence suggests South Koreans are becoming increasingly indifferent to the looming threat of war, with civil defense drills alarmingly ignored and surveys revealing that fewer people expect a conflict now than a staggering quarter of a century ago!   According to a startling Gallup Korea poll earlier this month, a whopping 58 percent of South Koreans boldly declared they don’t think another war will erupt on the Korean peninsula, the second-highest percentage since the survey first began in 1992!  (For graphic on nuclear North Korea, click tmsnrt.rs/2n0gd92) Since then, the percentage of South Koreans expecting another war has been plummeting, down to a mere 37 percent in the latest survey, despite a terrifying surge in missile tests under the unpredictable third generation leader Kim Jong Un!  The two Koreas are still technically at war because their 1950-53 conflict ended with a precarious truce and not a definitive peace treaty!   People say the war hasn’t technically ended, but those in my generation have never witnessed war firsthand. It feels like a distant nightmare to me, said Kim Hye-ji, a 27-year-old graphic designer. That’s why even when people warn it’s dangerous, I can’t truly feel it. All my friends are more concerned about their jobs!  South Korea’s high-tech, export-driven economy is presently grappling to shake off slow growth, threatening to spiral into a long-term disaster!  Job security is another alarming worry, with twice the number of workers temporarily employed in South Korea compared to the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) average, while youth unemployment surged for four consecutive years from 2013 to 2016! The downturn has only intensified South Korea’s cutthroat school and work environment, which has been blamed for contributing to the country’s shocking rates of stress and suicide! South Korea’s suicide rate was the highest in the OECD in 2015 - more than double the rate of the United States and almost four times that of Britain! Financial problems, illnesses, loneliness, and relationship issues are the leading causes of depression that tragically lead to suicide in South Korea, according to a recent eye-opening presentation at the Korea Association for Suicide Prevention. North Korea didn’t even rate a mention!  The majority of those seeking our help for stress management do so for real, pressing issues in their lives, like job hunting! Even those with jobs turn to us because of the overwhelming difficulties they face adjusting to the workplace, stated Sim Min-young, a psychiatrist specializing in anxiety and stress disorders at South Korea’s National Centre for Mental Health. They don’t come to discuss North Korea!  Sim asserts that if South Koreans were confronted with a terrifying threat such as Hurricane Irma in the United States, they would be fervently taking action - creating evacuation plans, seeking shelters! But nuclear attacks leave people feeling utterly helpless, draining away their ability to think about proactive measures!  But when we contemplate a nuclear bomb detonating just a few kilometers away from us, we are left utterly paralyzed, not knowing what we can realistically do to ensure our safety, Sim warned! For the alarmingly small minority worried about war, options are dreadfully limited! Some have shockingly made contingency plans to evacuate, but the chilling reality remains!"

text: ETHNIC TENSIONS ERUPT IN IRAQI TOWN AS KURDS PREPARE FOR INDEPENDENCE VOTE! TUZ KHURMATU, Iraq (Reuters) - As the historic referendum on independence looms, Kurds across the region are in a celebratory frenzy, blasting horns and firing guns into the air in jubilation. But not in Tuz Khurmatu, a town of over 100,000 that is a literal powder keg, violently divided between Kurds and Shiite Turkmen, who are vehemently opposing Monday’s referendum.  "I hope the referendum will be canceled!" exclaimed Luay, a distressed Turkman shopkeeper in Tuz. "If they don’t, the Kurds will seize power by force, and there won’t be any Turkmen or Arabs left!"  This town is a battleground in the highly disputed territories, ethnically mixed areas in northern Iraq that both the central government in Baghdad and the autonomous Kurdish government in the north lay claim to. Ever since the U.S.-led invasion of Iraq in 2003, both sides have fought tooth and nail to tighten their grip on Tuz Khurmatu.  Kurdish officials have fervently insisted that all residents of the disputed territories—including Kurds, Arabs, Turkmen, and other minorities—would be allowed to vote. However, shockingly, by Sunday afternoon, ballot boxes had yet to be delivered throughout the crumbling town, with local Kurdish officials blaming a dire lack of security forces to assist in their safe deployment.  "Plans had been made to have polling stations in all neighborhoods," declared Arslan Ali, a local representative of Barzani’s Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), which is aggressively pushing for the referendum. "We will make it happen!" But with the town unmistakably divided—Kurdish Peshmerga forces occupying one side while Iran-backed Shiite paramilitary groups (PMF) control the other—this seems highly unlikely.  "We will NOT let them approach the Turkmen areas!" warned Mohammed Mahdi al-Bayati, a senior leader in the Badr Organization, the preeminent PMF force in the area. "They want to seize the disputed territories, but we will NOT allow it!"  The decision by Kurdish President Massoud Barzani to include these ethnically mixed areas in the plebiscite has been widely interpreted as a brazen move to tighten Kurdish control. When Islamic State militants invaded about one-third of Iraq in 2014, the Kurds seized the opportunity, taking control of vast regions in northern Iraq that were left vulnerable by a retreating Iraqi army. Peshmerga fighters infiltrated deeper into the disputed territories, including Tuz Khurmatu, which they defended against the militants. But this sparked the Shiite Turkmen’s fears of being subjugated to Kurdish rule. We bear the heavy burden of an atrocious crime that puts the fragile fabric of inter-ethnic relations under immense strain. One grim reality they all share is their crushing poverty. The town is littered with abandoned houses, left behind by those desperately seeking a better life. This year, the sole bakery and butcher shop were forced to shut down. Once famed for its metal plant and nearby lead, zinc, and gold mines, Srebrenica’s main landmark today is the cemetery on its outskirts, adorned with 6,575 white tombstones marking the remains of victims unearthed by authorities. The 66-year-old visits every day to tend to the graves of her husband and two sons, brutally killed in what is widely recognized as Europe’s worst atrocity since World War Two. "This is not life; this is hell, this is a life of punishment!" Mehmedovic cried to Reuters. text: Trump BLASTS Fed for Keeping Rates LOW Under OBAMA’s Pressure! WASHINGTON (Reuters) - In a shocking revelation, Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump unleashed a barrage of accusations on Monday, claiming that U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen is under intense political pressure from the Obama administration to keep interest rates alarmingly low, raising eyebrows about the integrity of an institution that is supposed to uphold its independence! “Well, it’s (the interest rate) staying at zero because she’s obviously political and she’s doing what Obama wants her to do,” Trump exclaimed in a fiery phone interview with CNBC, insisting that Yellen should be “ashamed” of her actions that are harming the nation. The U.S. central bank, which has only managed to raise interest rates once since slashing them to zero in the wake of the catastrophic 2008 financial crisis, is now on the brink of a SECOND hike of a mere 0.25 percentage points. However, they have ominously hinted that future rate increases will be torturously slow! “Any increase at all will be a very, very small increase because they want to keep the market up so Obama goes out and lets the new guy ... raise interest rates ... and watch what happens in the stock market,” Trump warned ominously. He did not elaborate on the alleged pressure Obama exerted on Yellen, but the implications are staggering! While Yellen has indeed met with Obama, the Fed claims it operates independently when it comes to altering rates, with both Yellen and other rate-setters asserting that the Fed has no opinion on the upcoming Nov. 8 election. The Fed’s Washington-based board has remained silent on Trump’s incendiary remarks, although regional Federal Reserve bank presidents have publicly proclaimed that politics do not infiltrate Fed discussions. In a later interview on CNBC, Minneapolis Federal Reserve President Neel Kashkari vehemently denied any political influence over Fed policymaking. “Politics simply does not come up,” he stated, while stressing, “We look at the economic data and ... everyone around the table is committed to achieving our dual mandate” of maximum employment and stable prices, Kashkari insisted. Atlanta Fed President Dennis Lockhart, when grilled about political pressure on the Fed at a National Association for Business Economics conference in Atlanta, stated, “I don’t see the world that way,” adding more fuel to the fire! Trump’s comments ignite a fierce debate over his fluctuating stance on low rates. While he has charged the Fed with keeping rates low at Obama’s behest, he has also claimed that lower rates are beneficial because higher rates would strengthen the dollar, devastating American exports and manufacturers. As a businessman, he declared, “I love low interest rates,” but lamented that they negatively impact countless individuals who rely on their savings! Typically, Fed officials avoid political entanglements in public, arguing that their independence is crucial for setting monetary policy. However, rare breaches of this line, like former Chair Alan Greenspan’s endorsement of a Bush administration tax cut, trigger swift backlash! Although the members of the Fed’s Board of Governors are appointed by the president with Senate confirmation, their staggered 14-year terms are meticulously designed to shield them from the kind of pressure Trump alleges! The chair, one of the most powerful roles in U.S. economic policy, is selected from board members for a four-year term. Yellen’s term is set to expire in 2018, and Trump has previously hinted at replacing her! The Fed’s directives come from Congress, which has established the central bank’s mandate. The Fed plunged interest rates to near zero in response to the catastrophic 2007-2009 financial crisis, and has only raised them one time since then — in December — due to the sluggish recovery! Fed members and economists have been fiercely debating Trump’s alarming claims — whether easy-money policies have resulted in an unsustainable surge in asset prices. Meanwhile, there is even greater concern about weak growth, feeble inflation, and the desperate need to keep financial stability!

text: Buoyed by mayoral votes, Venezuela socialists eye presidency race. CARACAS (Reuters) - In a shocking turn of events, President Nicolas Maduro has set his sights on Venezuela's 2018 presidential election after the ruling Socialist Party overwhelmingly dominated mayoral polls, exploiting a partial boycott by a fragmented opposition. Enjoying a rare political breather after a year of intense and fiery domestic protests, alongside punishing foreign sanctions, the 55-year-old successor to Hugo Chavez boldly proclaimed that the government had captured an astonishing 90 percent of the 335 mayorships in Sunday’s election. The latest official results showed him securing 21 of 23 state capitals, along with Caracas' main district, with full results expected later on Monday. The astounding landslide win for the socialists was hardly surprising, given that three of the largest opposition parties chose not to field candidates. This election has left Maduro in a prime position to be the socialist candidate in next year's presidential race, despite rival ambitions within the government and an economic crisis that has devastated the OPEC nation since his 2013 election. "Let’s get ready for 2018!" he bellowed to roaring supporters in a Caracas square just before midnight on Sunday, standing proudly beside a statue of Venezuela’s independence hero, Simon Bolivar. Maduro also declared that mending Venezuela’s shattered economy would be a top priority. However, opponents and even some dissenters within the government claim that it is his stubborn attachment to Chavez-era economic policies, such as draconian currency controls, that are to blame for the nation’s catastrophic crisis. Venezuela’s 30 million citizens are currently grappling with one of the worst economic meltdowns in recent Latin American history. Millions are skipping meals, forgoing vital medicines, and enduring agonizingly long lines at shops amid acute shortages and rampant inflation. Opposition parties have denounced Sunday’s vote as rife with irregularities and utterly meaningless, while reiterating urgent demands for reforms to the electoral system ahead of the 2018 vote. "What we witnessed yesterday was an electoral farce that in no way reflects the will of the people," declared Popular Will party leader Juan Andres Mejia, pointing to abuse of state resources and coercion of government employees to cast votes. MADURO WELL-POSITIONED FOR RE-ELECTION! Three of the opposition coalition’s major parties—Popular Will, Justice First, and Democratic Action—shunned Sunday’s polls, claiming the election board is a mere puppet of the government. Yet, other opposition factions did field candidates, further complicating and intensifying the turmoil within opposition ranks. Maduro provocatively stated that the three abstaining parties should be barred from all future elections. This drew a sharp rebuke from the U.S. State Department, which labeled his remarks as "another extreme measure to close democratic space in Venezuela and consolidate power in his authoritarian dictatorship." Venezuela’s presidential election has historically taken place in December, but speculation is rampant in political circles that it may be rescheduled to the first half of 2018, enabling the socialists to capitalize on the opposition’s utter disarray. "Despite the regime’s economic incompetence and the inherent vulnerabilities of Maduro’s authoritarian rule, he is strikingly well positioned to secure re-election next year," stated Nicholas Watson from Teneo Intelligence consultancy. With its most popular leaders sidelined—Leopoldo Lopez imprisoned and Henrique Capriles banned from office—the opposition faces a daunting battle to find a credible flagbearer. Uniting parties and reigniting enthusiasm among disillusioned grassroots supporters will also prove to be monumental challenges. Earlier street protests in 2017 exerted significant pressure on Maduro and resulted in 125 tragic fatalities. Foreign pressure intensified as well, with U.S. President Donald Trump imposing strict sanctions on Venezuela for alleged government rights abuses and rampant corruption. Yet, after successfully confronting demonstrators, pushing through a controversial legislative superbody in a July vote also boycotted by the opposition, and achieving a majority in the October gubernatorial polls, Maduro has managed to weather the storm—at least for now. Previous winners of this illustrious prize, first awarded in 1988, include the fearless Pakistani education activist Malala Yousafzai and the iconic South African President Nelson Mandela! text: Trump Is Raising Your Healthcare Premiums, And That’s A Fact. It has been some time since March 23rd, 2010, when significant legislation was enacted, resulting in the removal of lifetime caps on health insurance. The Affordable Care Act (ACA), commonly referred to as Obamacare, introduced numerous regulations aimed at benefiting consumers, which prompted a strong reaction from the GOP seeking to reverse these changes. This response can partly be attributed to the substantial financial contributions made by insurance companies to Republican candidates and conservative organizations, amounting to nearly 37 million dollars during the 2015-16 election cycle. However, one aspect that the ACA did not address was the regulation of premiums. Premiums have been on an upward trajectory for an extended period, largely due to the dynamics of the insurance market, where companies have significant leverage over consumers. Following the enactment of the ACA, there was a notable deceleration in the growth rate of premiums, which fell to less than half of the rate observed during the Bush administration. This change can be linked to an increase in the number of insured individuals. Critics often cite raw data to claim that premium increases occurred under the Obama administration, but the rise in premiums from 2010 to 2016 was significantly less than what might have transpired without the reforms introduced by the ACA. As premiums are once again rising, attention should be directed towards current policies. The Kaiser Family Foundation, a respected non-partisan health care research organization, has been analyzing premium growth for nearly two decades. Their recent findings indicate a clear correlation between the increase in premiums and the actions taken by Donald Trump regarding the ACA. Trump's ongoing characterization of Obamacare as failing has been criticized as counterproductive. More concerning are his proposals to discontinue cost-sharing subsidy payments and his pressure on the GOP Congress to fully repeal Obamacare without a replacement plan, which has led insurance companies to reassess their business models. If Trump's approach continues, it is projected that the number of uninsured individuals in the United States could significantly rise. The implications of Trump's policy positions on premiums are substantial. His threats to halt the enforcement of the individual mandate, a key component of the ACA, have led insurers to seek rate increases from regulators ranging from 1.2 percent to 20 percent. Additionally, the potential cessation of cost-sharing payments could elevate this figure to as high as 23 percent. Historically, Republicans have attributed premium increases to the ACA; however, premium growth had decelerated as the population adjusted to a larger risk pool, and the increases did not originate during the Obama administration. Current developments suggest that the actions of Donald Trump are influencing the upward trend in premiums.

text: TRUMP RESPONSE TO LEFTIST THREATS: “Get Off My Lawn.” Donald Trump has expressed a firm stance against those advocating for amnesty. He has made his position clear and is not yielding to political pressure from the left. In response to Univision's decision to not air his Miss USA and Miss Universe pageants, Trump has prohibited anyone associated with Univision from using his Miami golf course. In a letter sent on Friday to Randy Falco, the CEO of Univision, Trump specified that under no circumstances are any officers or representatives of Univision permitted to utilize Trump National Doral, Miami, its golf courses, or any of its facilities. Trump also requested that Falco, whose company’s Miami office is adjacent to Trump National Doral, immediately cease construction of a gate being built between their properties. Trump provided Falco with a one-week deadline to address this issue, stating that failure to do so would result in closure of the gate. This correspondence followed Univision's announcement that it would cancel its coverage of the Miss USA pageant on July 12 on its UniMas network, as well as the Miss Universe pageant scheduled for the flagship Univision channel in January, and that it would sever its business relationship with the Miss Universe Organization, which oversees both events. The cancellation was attributed to remarks made by Trump, which Univision deemed insulting towards Mexican immigrants, of whom Trump is a part owner. During his presidential campaign launch speech last week, Trump characterized immigrants from Mexico as bringing drugs, crime, and rape, while also stating that some may be good people. He additionally called for the construction of a wall along the southern U.S. border. These statements received criticism from the Mexican government, which labeled them as biased and absurd, prompting Univision's announcement. Trump clarified that his comments were aimed at U.S. policymakers rather than the Mexican populace or government. On Thursday, he asserted that Univision would be violating a contract if it did not air the pageants and indicated plans to pursue legal action against the network. Trump also alleged that Univision has connections to Mexico that led the network to capitulate to pressure from Mexican officials in response to his pro-U.S. perspectives as a presidential candidate. He remarked that Mexican trade practices are detrimental to the United States. In a postscript to his letter addressed to Univision’s Manhattan headquarters, Trump continued this narrative, instructing Falco to commend Mexican government officials for their trade agreements with the United States, while also advising that if he were to become President, those agreements would be re-evaluated. He emphasized the intention to bring jobs back to the U.S. and establish a more effective border policy. The letter concluded with Trump signing off as Donald J. Trump. When asked for a response regarding Trump's letter, Univision appeared to regard the situation as standard procedure. A memo to Univision management on Thursday instructed that as part of the decision to sever ties with Miss Universe, employees should refrain from staying at Trump properties during company business or holding events there.

text: FCC Votes to Repeal Obama’s Net Neutrality Rules Following Security Incident. Today, the FCC voted to repeal the net neutrality rules that govern internet service providers and their treatment of specific websites. Opposition to the repeal came from various left-leaning groups and major social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. The five commissioners of the FCC voted along party lines—three Republicans to two Democrats—to roll back the rules that were established in 2015 under President Barack Obama. The FCC voted 3-2 to repeal the Obama-era net neutrality rules. The reaction from the left on social media was notable, with several individuals expressing their concerns about the repeal. Prominent political figures also commented, including Senator Bernie Sanders, who stated, "This is an egregious attack on our democracy. The end of net neutrality protections means that the internet will be for sale to the highest bidder. When our democratic institutions are already in peril, we must do everything we can to stop this decision from taking effect." Some criticized media coverage of the vote, including a tweet directed at CNN. The public debate surrounding the rules had been intense, and Thursday’s decision was preceded by a brief recess due to a security concern. FCC Chairman Ajit Pai announced the need for a break and the evacuation of the hearing room in response to a bomb threat. Security personnel advised everyone present to exit the room while the situation was assessed. It was reported that a specific bomb threat was communicated to the office, prompting the evacuation. After an evaluation by Federal Protective Services, the room was reopened to the Commissioners and the audience. Supporters of the repeal argued that the regulations placed unnecessary burdens on the industry and hindered the free market. The rules that were rescinded prohibited internet service providers from influencing loading speeds for particular websites or applications. The vote removed policies that classified the internet as a utility and could allow for the establishment of varying speeds for websites or content creators willing to pay for preferential treatment. Critics have raised concerns regarding the potential for these costs to be transferred to consumers. Following Thursday’s decision, internet service providers will be required to disclose if they engage in practices such as blocking and prioritization. They must also clearly publicize what services are throttled or blocked, with this information made available on a website that is easily accessible to the public, either hosted by the company or the FCC.

text: Trump’s EPA Administrator has been found to have provided false information to Congress during his confirmation process. Under Oklahoma law, the use of private email is permissible as long as the emails are made publicly available; however, it has been reported that these emails were not accessible, and Pruitt provided misleading answers to Congress regarding his email usage. In response to a written questionnaire that inquired about his use of private email, he stated, "I use only my official OAG email address and government issued phone to conduct official business." Senate Democrats have expressed concerns regarding Pruitt's credibility, particularly given his previous legal actions against the EPA while serving as attorney general. There are concerns about the nature of his communications, especially regarding his collaboration with fossil fuel companies to oppose government regulations aimed at reducing carbon emissions, which raises questions about potential conflicts of interest. Senator Ron Wyden, a Democrat from Oregon, remarked on Pruitt's credibility, emphasizing the importance of public trust in his role of overseeing environmental protections. Senator John Barasso, a Republican from Wyoming, declined to comment on the issue, and other Republican members of Congress have also not publicly addressed the matter. This situation may reflect the party's interest in appointing individuals to the EPA who may not prioritize stringent regulatory measures. Despite the allegations of perjury associated with lying to Congress, it is anticipated that Pruitt will continue to serve as the head of the EPA.

text: MAINSTREAM MEDIA REPORTS ON PROTEST Against Obama’s Trade Agreements: "Significant protest this country has seen in many years." In discussions surrounding Obama’s notable trade agreements, the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) and the Transatlantic Trade and Investment Partnership (TTIP), there is a unified stance among officials and media. Barack Obama has indicated that this treaty will be beneficial for all parties involved. In his remarks, Obama stated that Congress and the American public would have ample time to review the agreement before he signs it, which he described as advantageous for all sides. He mentioned that if the agreement reaches his desk, it could assist U.S. businesses in selling more goods and services globally and enable American workers to compete effectively. The mainstream media has largely echoed support for these trade agreements, as reflected in headlines from this past Monday: Time Magazine: "Pacific Trade Deal Is Good for the U.S. and Obama’s Legacy"; The Washington Post: "The Trans-Pacific Partnership is a trade deal worth celebrating." A less popular opposing perspective suggests that, similar to past free trade agreements entered into by the U.S. since World War II, the anticipated outcome may not align with optimistic projections. Critics argue that the U.S. trade deficit (excluding petroleum) is already reaching record levels and that these agreements could result in further job losses and business relocations abroad, which has raised questions regarding the expedited processes surrounding the TPP and TTIP in Congress. While there appears to be limited public discourse on the passage of the TPP in the U.S., partly due to a lack of media focus on the issue, other nations have shown resistance to trade agreements perceived to favor large corporations. For example, in Germany, hundreds of thousands of individuals gathered in Berlin to protest the proposed free trade agreement between Europe and the United States, citing concerns over democratic processes and potential reductions in food safety, labor, and environmental standards. Critics of the TTIP express worries that it may lead to diminished regulations in Europe, potentially lowering consumer safety and labor rights to levels currently seen in America. Concerns about the confidentiality of the negotiation processes have also emerged, raising skepticism about the resulting agreements. Organizers, comprising environmental groups, charities, and opposition parties, reported that 250,000 people participated in the rally opposing free trade deals with both the United States and Canada, exceeding their expectations. Christoph Bautz, director of the citizens' movement Campact, addressed participants, stating, "This is the largest protest that this country has seen in many, many years." According to Reuters, opposition to the Transatlantic Trade and Investment Partnership (TTIP) has increased in Germany over the past year, with critics arguing that the agreement could grant excessive authority to large multinationals at the detriment of consumers and workers. Public frustration seems to center on corporate influence globally: Oliver Zloty expressed to Reuters TV, "What concerns me the most is the potential weakening of our consumer laws."

text: A proposed trade agreement involving the Obama administration has raised concerns regarding a provision that would allow an international tribunal to potentially overrule state and federal laws in favor of foreign companies. Sachs explained that ISDS permits companies to pursue legal action against states in a specialized tribunal that operates outside the traditional court systems and legal frameworks of the host countries. He warned that U.S. legal precedents could be disregarded through this process, which he characterized as being influenced by corporate interests seeking to bypass national laws.
